```c
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_new(bennett_sched_request_t** out);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_object(bennett_sched_request_t*, const uint8_t*, size_t);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_target(bennett_sched_request_t*, const uint8_t* jcs, size_t);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_region(bennett_sched_request_t*, const char* closure_hash_hex, const char* variant, uint32_t inherited_controls);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_budget(bennett_sched_request_t*, uint64_t steps, uint64_t heap, uint64_t stack, uint64_t depth);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_params(bennett_sched_request_t*, const uint8_t* params_jcs, size_t);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_accuracy(bennett_sched_request_t*, const char* epsilon_decimal);
bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_capacity(bennett_sched_request_t*, const char* cls, uint64_t peak_qubits);
void           bennett_sched_request_free(bennett_sched_request_t*);
bennett_status bennett_sched_schedule(const bennett_sched_request_t*, bennett_sched_response_t** out);
typedef enum { BENNETT_SCHED_OK, BENNETT_SCHED_INFEASIBLE, BENNETT_SCHED_UNSUPPORTED } bennett_sched_outcome;
bennett_sched_outcome bennett_sched_response_outcome(const bennett_sched_response_t*);
const char*    bennett_sched_response_reason(const bennett_sched_response_t*);
const uint8_t* bennett_sched_response_schedule(const bennett_sched_response_t*, size_t* len);
const uint8_t* bennett_sched_response_certificate(const bennett_sched_response_t*, size_t* len);
void           bennett_sched_response_free(bennett_sched_response_t*);
```

**Generated operations and the expansion library.** Every row and
instruction expands into **generated operations** (gates, allocations,
releases). Above gate level the order is fixed by §3.6, §4.2, §4.5–§4.6
and §5.2 (dispatch comparators k = 0..n in index order; a row's
sub-operations in listed order; successor XORs; commit; cleanup). Below
that level (the gate decomposition of comparators, adders, multiplexers,
`inrange` scans and their scratch) the expansion is defined by an
**expansion library**: a versioned document, identified in the
schedule's `bindings.expansion` as `{ "name", "version", "hash" }`, that
lists for every row kind and every instruction its generated operations
in order, with their **ordinals**, scratch identities and the subset it
marks removable, and that is extensionally equal to the reference (§5.7,
T6). A consumer that does not implement the bound library rejects the
schedule (`E_SCHEDULE_INFEASIBLE`); two consumers implementing it
execute and charge the same operation set. `bennett-isa-spec` publishes
the reference library `ref` (§17 item 7). §5.7 transformations under a
schedule MUST keep the ordinals of the operations they keep and MAY
remove only operations the library marks removable.

**Schedule document** (JCS):

```
  { "bindings": { "closure_hash", "target_hash", "region", "variant", "inherited_controls", "budget": [B,heap,stack,depth],
                  "params_hash", "epsilon", "expansion": { "name", "version", "hash" }, "scheduler": { "name", "version" } },
    "entries": [ { "path": [ { "symbol": hex, "point": "<block>:<ordinal>", "iteration": [n, …] | "*" }, … ],
                   "step": n | "*",  "phase": "fwd" | "rev" | "*",  "generated": n | "*",
                   "kind": "cleanup" | "gate" | "alloc" | "start",
                   "cleanup": { "realisation": "reverse" | "recompute" },
                   "gate":    { "realisation": "native" | "<scheme name>", "epsilon_share": decimal },
                   "alloc":   { "class": "<cls>" },           /* a concrete class; "any" is not allowed in a schedule */
                   "start":   { "time": decimal } } ] }
```

**Matching.** Every generated operation has an **invocation chain**: the
program points of the region calls, `lift.call`s and `lift.oracle_call`s
that led to it, outermost first, ending in its own point. `path` matches
an operation iff it is a **prefix** of that chain, element by element:
`symbol` and `point` equal, and `iteration` either `*` or equal to the
vector of 0-based dynamic repetition counts of the `qloop`s enclosing
that point (outermost first; its length is the point's loop nesting
depth, `[]` outside every loop). `step` is the forward machine step t ∈
1..B of an oracle-generated operation (`phase: rev` denotes the inverse
of step t; both are per invocation level, so a nested oracle's step is
selected by a path element for the nested call); `generated` is the
ordinal within the row's expansion in the bound library. **Specificity**
is the lexicographic tuple (path length, number of non-`*` iterations,
step non-`*`, phase non-`*`, generated non-`*`); an entry applies to a
generated operation iff all its selectors match; among matching entries
the unique maximal one applies; **two incomparable maximal matching
entries make the schedule invalid** (document order is never
significant). Selectors are resolved independently per `kind`. Defaults
for uncovered operations: `reverse`; `native` if the gate matches a
`gates` entry, else the first matching scheme; class = the first class
declared in the target's `classes` object (JCS order) that has capacity
for it; sequential timing in generated order. **Timing**: a `start` time
MUST be ≥ the end of every operation the operation depends on (data,
wire lifetime, region cell version, effect order); an entry violating
this makes the schedule invalid. **Obligations**: satisfy §6; respect
capacity; report every resource; be reproducible from the request plus
scheduler version. A consumer validates every binding and every path
against the object and executes verbatim or rejects (`E_SCHEDULE_
INFEASIBLE`).

## 12. Certificate (cert 0.8; JCS)

### 12.1 Claims

| kind | payload | checker obligation |
|---|---|---|
| `exhaustive` | `domain` (§12.2); `expected`: `"oracle"` \| `{ "table": [...] }` \| `{ "program": closure_hash }` | re-execute every domain element on the reference interpreter / expected program; compare full tuples |
| `sampled` | `domain`; `sampler`: `{ "algorithm": "xoshiro256**", "seed": [4 decimal strings, not all zero], "count": n }` | replay; **evidence** |
| `structural` | `{ "rule": "translation_lemma" \| "inverse_pair_library" \| "adjoint_table", "subclaims": [indices], "witness": … }`; for `translation_lemma`: `{ "V": [points], "W": [points], "X": [wires], "B": [wires], "frame": [first point, last point] }`; for `inverse_pair_library`: `{ "library_closure_hash", "claim_index" }`; for `adjoint_table`: `{}` | check the rule's side conditions syntactically against the object and the subclaims' results |
| `numerical` | `{ "subject": { "closure_hash", "variant", "inherited_controls", "schedule_hash" }, "metric": "operator_norm", "precision_bits": n, "bound": decimal }` | **checker-computed, for every invocation context of the subject** (below): build the realised unitary U of that invocation (the region's realisation under the root schedule at that path, with its resolved classical arguments, budget, epsilon shares and cleanup choices, and `inherited_controls` control wires prepended) and the reference unitary V (the region's §5.3 semantics with the same arguments, controlled on the same wires) at the subject's signature widths in interval arithmetic at `precision_bits` (basis order = allocation order, controls first), form interval enclosures of `V†U − I` entrywise, derive the operator-norm bound as the Frobenius-norm upper bound in interval arithmetic, and verify it is ≤ `bound`; the claim holds iff it holds for every context |
| `channel` | `{ "subject": as above, "metric": "diamond", "precision_bits", "bound", "dual": [ { "Y": interval Hermitian matrix, "mu": decimal } … ] }` | for every invocation context of the subject, in enumeration order, verify its dual witness for the **diamond-norm SDP** below in interval arithmetic and `mu` ≤ `bound` (one witness per context; too few witnesses: reject) |

**Invocation contexts.** A subject denotes the set of invocations of
the region `closure_hash`, with the given `variant` and `inherited_
controls`, in the root schedule `schedule_hash`: every path of that
schedule's region tree reaching the region, with the classical
arguments, budget, `epsilon_share`s and cleanup realisations resolved
at that path. Contexts are enumerated in path order (the schedule's
`entries` paths sorted bytewise as JCS). Every claim bound and every
`error` entry (§12.3) is a **common upper bound over all contexts** of
its key; the multiplicity composition of §12.3 is sound for that reason.

**Diamond-norm SDP** (Watrous, *Theory of Computing* 5 (2009), §4; the
Hermiticity-preserving simplification). Let Φ = Φ_real − Φ_ref be the
difference of the subject's realised channel and the reference channel
(both on the subject's interface, controls included), d_in = d_out = d
the dimension. The **Choi matrix** is J(Φ) = Σ_{i,j} |i⟩⟨j| ⊗ Φ(|i⟩⟨j|)
(input factor first, output factor second, computational basis in
allocation order, **unnormalised**). The witness is a Hermitian Y of
dimension d² and a decimal mu. The checker accepts iff, with every
matrix entry an interval and every test rigorous (an inconclusive test
rejects): Y − J(Φ) ⪰ 0, Y + J(Φ) ⪰ 0, mu·I − Tr_out(Y) ⪰ 0 (partial trace
over the output factor), and mu ≤ `bound`; then ‖Φ‖◇ ≤ mu (the dual of
Watrous's SDP with Y₀ = Y₁ = Y; this is the diamond norm itself, not
half of it). Encoding: `Y` is a row-major array of entries `[re_lo, re_
hi, im_lo, im_hi]` (decimal strings). **Positivity test.** The checker
proves each of the three matrices **positive definite** by an interval
Cholesky (or Hermitian LDL†) factorisation in which the interval lower
bound of every pivot is strictly positive, and rejects otherwise; no
other test is admitted (nonnegative leading principal minors do not
imply positive semidefiniteness: diag(0, −1)). Producers make witnesses
strictly feasible by replacing Y with Y + δI and mu with mu′ = mu + δ·(d
+ 1) for a small rational δ > 0 (any mu′ > mu + δ·d suffices): then Y ±
J(Φ) ⪰ δI ≻ 0 and, since Tr_out(Y + δI) = Tr_out(Y) + δ·d·I, mu′·I −
Tr_out(Y + δI) ⪰ δI ≻ 0; ‖Φ‖◇ ≤ mu′, which MUST be ≤ `bound`. **Interval
arithmetic** at `precision_bits`
means every operation rounds outward to `precision_bits`-bit binary
rationals; transcendental entries (`rx ry rz`) are enclosed by a Taylor
series with the Lagrange remainder bound (§17 item 8 fixes the term
count). The subject's `schedule_hash` is required: an executable claim
names the realisation it is about.

**Sampling.** For each domain component with range size R = hi − lo + 1,
assemble m = ⌈⌈log₂ R⌉/64⌉ consecutive generator words (least-significant
word first) into an integer, reduce modulo 2^⌈log₂ R⌉, reject and redraw
if ≥ R, add `lo`; components are consumed in enumeration order.

### 12.2 Domains

`"domain": { "bundles": [ { "name", "width", "lo", "hi" } ], "borrowed": [ same ], "regions": [ { "name", "cells": "all" | [ { "index", "lo", "hi" } ] } ] }`,
bounds inclusive, enumeration order as listed, last component fastest.
A `proof` label requires the domain to equal D; otherwise the claim is
`evidence` with the covered fraction.

### 12.3 Schema and composition

```
  versions; bindings { object_hash, interface_hash, closure_hash (required), reference_program_hash, dialect_mapping_version, target_hash, schedule_hash? }
  producer { name, version, materialisation { llvm_version, pipeline, normaliser_version } }
  regions { <closure_hash>: { kind, signature, bounds, frame (§9.4), resources { name: decimal }, gates_used { gate: { count, scheme?, epsilon? } },
            claims: [ <claim> … ], verification: { oracle: i, borrow_frames: [i], inverse_pairs: [ { g, ginv, claim: i } ], unitary: [i], channel: [i],
                                                   fault_rate: { domain, faults_by_code, undefined_excluded, layout_dependent_excluded } },
            cleanup: { "<variant>:<inherited_controls>": [ { path, realisation } ] },
            error:   { "<variant>:<inherited_controls>": { local: { "operator_norm"?: v, "diamond"?: v }, inclusive: { "operator_norm"?: v, "diamond"?: v } } },
            definedness_assumptions: [ids] } }
  composition { multiplicities: { "<hash>:<variant>:<inherited_controls>": n (from the realised schedule) }, epsilon_total: { "diamond": v }, method: "sum_over_multiplicities" }
```

`inclusive(R, key) = local(R, key) + Σ_callees n_c × inclusive(c, key_c)`
**per metric**, keyed like `cleanup` by `<variant>:<inherited_controls>`
(the realised error depends on both); every `local` value is a verified
common upper bound over all invocation contexts of its key in the bound
root schedule (§12.1), so multiplying by n_c is sound; an
`operator_norm` value converts
to `diamond` by ×2 once, at the point it is first combined with a
`diamond` value; `operator_norm` conclusions (T6, controlled unitary
variants) require `operator_norm` bounds throughout. A controlled
unitary variant requires a `numerical` claim; an ε > 0 realisation
compared as a channel requires a `channel` claim. Executable claims
(`numerical`, `channel`, `exhaustive` with `expected: "oracle"`) bind to
`schedule_hash` through their subject.

## 13. Coverage (coverage 0.8)

`{ "entries": [ { "point": <program-point id>, "source": "<dialect-spec stable id>", "classification": "lowered" | "trapped" | "shimmed", "reason", "fault_code"?, "shim_hash"?, "count" } ] }`.

## 14. Formal model

### 14.1 Reference interpreter *(normative)*

Executes an oracle's reference body per basis configuration: locations
and cells are bit-vectors, pseudo-locations read-only, predication is
`if`, each §4.2 row is its classical function (including the inherent
`inrange` check of loads and stores, the activation records of §3.7, the
`alloctab` and stack arrays), `fault` records the code and halts, `lift.
retval` halts with success and `f(x) = result_val`, the step counter
counts executed rows, counters are unbounded integers. It **defines** F_B
and the budget unit and rejects any body that executes a non-permutation
gate.

### 14.2 Quantum state semantics

The state of a Q region is a vector in ⊗ over live wires in allocation
order (bundles little-endian). `qalloc` tensors |0⟩; `qfree` removes
clean factors; `qborrow` introduces a factor in unknown state possibly
entangled with a reference system R, and the region's operation must be
U ⊗ I on it (§5.6); gates act by §4.4 under the active predicate;
`measure` (CC) is the projective computational-basis measurement with
Born probabilities, consuming the wires.

### 14.3 Theorems

- **T1 (totality).** For every well-formed oracle, budget and x ∈ D the
  reference interpreter halts within B + 1 rows and F_B(x) is unique.
- **T2 (prefix reversal).** For every executor whose realisation is a
  composition of ε = 0 permutation gates implementing §5.2 steps 1–4
  with the inverse step of §3.6, on every x ∈ D every non-interface wire
  is clean after step 4 and borrowed bundles hold their initial values.
- **T3 (permutation theorem).** If the realised unitary V of a circuit on
  span(D) is a permutation matrix and the final basis tuple equals P(x)
  for every x ∈ D, then V|span(D) = P.
- **T4 (round trip).** For every finite valid CC/R trace with retained
  run history and tapes, LIFO reversal per §7.4 restores the classical
  environment, memory, allocation table, device-model state and history
  to entry values; observed external events are not retracted.
- **T5.** As §6.3.
- **T6 (executor agreement).** Two executors conforming to §3–§7 on one
  target with the same schedule produce on every x ∈ D the same final
  tuple for every oracle (exact) and, for every action with `operator_
  norm` inclusive bounds e₁, e₂, unitaries within e₁ + e₂ in operator
  norm; for channels, diamond bounds d₁ + d₂.

### 14.4 Mechanisation *(deferred)*

## 15. Conformance suites

| Suite | Class | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| A | Executor | classical ISA; run history and LIFO reversal with loops, recursion, effects, segment `uncall` (impure suffix traps; nested `uncall` inside an uncalled segment; `uncall` over a `measure` traps), `hostcall`, `qreg.*`, fault records (T4) |
| B | Executor | oracle totality and prefix reversal: every fault code; B = 0; boundary halts; `lift.call`/`lift.ret` recursion with argument capture; one forward `lift.call` and one forward `lift.ret` step of a recursive call each followed by its inverse (§3.7); stack exhaustion (`sp + R_f > stack_limit`); matched `lift.oracle_uncall`; interface regions restored; pre-entries; `lift.free` on pinned entries; inherent load/store checks |
| C | Executor, Producer | T3 over full D at exhaustive widths for oracles, permutation actions, `qinplace` pairs, borrow frames; T6 agreement among VM, specialiser, transformed forms and the reference interpreter; the §16.3 examples as normative test vectors, including the stack-capacity boundary of example 2 |
| D | Executor | channel and unitary comparison for ε > 0 realisations; controlled-interference tests; checker-computed bounds; the diamond-norm SDP witness check of §12.1 |
| E | Target author, Executor | JCS parsing; AST evaluation; matching; scheme expansion and correctness; aggregation from event lists; timing model; imports |
| F | Producer | versioning, disjointness incl. control context; operand schema; row classes and frame sizing; index-space flattening; terminators; name resolution; permutation-only oracles; §6 transfer and windows; adjoint table; translation lemma side conditions with the four negative tests; `in`-wire use; acyclic action graphs; grammar; schemas; envelope and hashes; linking; frame-descriptor live ranges |
| G | Launch | every §10 entry point, state transition, binding rule, ownership rule; HOST_REQUEST/reply; reverse eligibility and tree order |
| H | Scheduler | §6 validity; capacity; reproducibility; specificity resolution; verbatim execution; INFEASIBLE/UNSUPPORTED |

## 16. Canonical textual form (normative)

### 16.1 Lexical

UTF-8; LF line endings; one instruction per line; tokens separated by
exactly one space; no trailing spaces; exactly one blank line before
each `section` line and none elsewhere. `NAME := [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*`;
`INT := -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)`; `FLOAT :=` shortest round-trip decimal with
`.` or exponent, finite; `STRING := "…"` with escapes `\"`, `\\`, `\n`;
`HEX := ([0-9a-f]{2})*`. Metadata lines are RFC 8785 canonical JSON
objects.

### 16.2 Grammar

```
  object    := header NL section*
  header    := "bennett-object" SP "isa=" VER SP "object=" VER SP "launch=" VER SP "sched=" VER SP "cert=" VER SP "coverage=" VER SP "target=" VER SP "ptr_width=" INT
  section   := NL "section" SP SECTNAME NL body
  SECTNAME  := "symbols" | "imports" | "functions" | "data" | "devices" | "layout" | "schedule" | "certificate" | "coverage"
  body      := jsonline | dataline* | function*
  jsonline  := JCS-canonical JSON object NL
  dataline  := NAME SP HEX NL
  function  := fhead NL regs? block+
  fhead     := ("fn" SP ("cc"|"r") | "oracle" | "action" | "perm_action" | "lproc") SP "@" NAME SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")" SP "(" plist ")"
               -- oracle: (in..) (tgt) (fault) (mem..) (args..) ; action: (mut..) (in..) (mem..) (args..) () ; lproc: (params..) (result) () () () ; fn: (params..) (results..) () () ()
  plist     := (param ("," SP param)*)?
  param     := NAME ":" type (SP ("in"|"mut"))?
  type      := "i" INT | "ptr" | "f64" | "token" | "wire" | "wire[" INT "]" | "reg[" INT "]" | "region[" INT "," INT "]" | "qreg[" INT "]"
  regs      := "regs" SP "{" SP (NAME ":" type ("," SP NAME ":" type)*)? SP "}" (SP "bounds" SP "{" INT ("," SP INT)* "}")? NL
  block     := "^" NAME "(" plist "):" NL instr+
  instr     := (lhs SP "=" SP)? OPCODE (SP operand)* (SP "{" NL instr+ "}" (SP "{" NL instr+ "}")?)? NL
  lhs       := NAME | "(" NAME ("," SP NAME)* ")"
  operand   := NAME | NAME "[" INT "]" | "@" NAME | "^" NAME ("(" (NAME ("," SP NAME)*)? ")")? | INT | FLOAT | STRING | "(" (NAME ("," SP NAME)*)? ")"
  OPCODE    := a mnemonic of §4 with its dotted suffix (§4.8 fixes operand count, kinds and result placement)
  VER       := INT "." INT
```

### 16.3 Example objects (normative test vectors, suite C and F)

**Example 1** (`inc8`): one oracle, no lprocs, no memory. The function
has **six** canonical lines.

```
bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32

section symbols
{"0":{"interface_hash":"8ce5e64f15830d8e596ba9b4861def6565dd567b5804300f427d8b9566d5be93","kind":"oracle","name":"inc8","signature":{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}}}

section functions
oracle @inc8 (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()
regs { one:reg[8], r:reg[8] }
^entry():
one = lift.const.i8 1
r = lift.add x one
lift.retval r
```

The object has no `layout` section, so the oracle's closure set is
empty and its envelope is exactly these bytes (each line LF-terminated):

```
isa=0.8
ptr_width=32
{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}
oracle @inc8 (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()
regs { one:reg[8], r:reg[8] }
^entry():
one = lift.const.i8 1
r = lift.add x one
lift.retval r
```

With B ≥ 3 every x yields `(x + 1 mod 256, 0)` (`result_val` = 0 ⊕ r);
with B = 2 every x yields `(0, FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS)`.

**Example 2** (`sum_db`): an oracle reading an interface region through
lifted memory with a recursive lproc that receives the base as a
parameter, and a global accessed by address.

```
bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width=32

section symbols
{"0":{"interface_hash":"68225d213c44812fe844cd295d8821127c3cf31682be4eb19303cb53f9b147f7","kind":"oracle","name":"sum_db","signature":{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[{"A":4,"W":8,"role":"in"}],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}},"1":{"interface_hash":"74f110bbafde68a4785025e7e571ef871ddd83a09465ab9c1604f653a0cfcd92","kind":"lproc","name":"sum","signature":{"abi":"0.8","kind":"lproc","params":[8,8,32],"result":8,"tier":"q"}},"2":{"interface_hash":"7002ed5ea010907a0ae99065663f22fb7d18ca1d6cb171fed57e2594bd9367e6","kind":"data","name":"zero","signature":{"abi":"0.8","kind":"data","size":1,"tier":"-"}}}

section functions
oracle @sum_db (n:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) (db:region[4,8] in) ()
regs { base:reg[32], acc:reg[8], r:reg[8] }
^entry():
base = lift.addr @db
acc = lift.const.i8 0
r = lift.call @sum (n, acc, base)
lift.retval r
lproc @sum (n:reg[8], acc:reg[8], base:reg[32]) (r:reg[8]) () () ()
regs { zp:reg[32], zv:reg[8], z:reg[1], one:reg[8], n2:reg[8], idx:reg[32], p:reg[32], v:reg[8], acc2:reg[8] }
^entry():
zp = lift.addr @zero
lift.boundscheck zp 1
zv = lift.load.i8 zp
z = lift.icmp.eq n zv
qbranch z ^done ^more
^more():
one = lift.const.i8 1
n2 = lift.sub n one
idx = lift.zext.i32 n2
p = lift.add base idx
lift.boundscheck p 1
v = lift.load.i8 p
acc2 = lift.add acc v
r = lift.call @sum (n2, acc2, base)
lift.ret r
^done():
lift.ret acc

section data
zero 00

section layout
{"A_tab":4,"H":13,"S_cells":9,"globals":{"zero":{"base":16,"image":"zero","size":1}},"heap_base":4112,"heap_limit_max":4080,"interface_regions":{"sum_db":{"db":{"base":4096}}},"null_size":16,"ptr_width":32}
```

Ranges: null [0,16), `zero` [16,17), `db` [4096,4112), heap [4112,8192)
within 2^13: disjoint; two pre-entries ≤ 2^4. `alloctab` starts with
pinned entries (16,1) and (4096,16), `atop = 2`. `@sum` resolves `n acc
base` to its params and everything else to its own locations; its
locations are `n acc base` (params), `r` (result name), then its nine
`regs`: m′ = 13, **R_sum = 16 cells**; `@sum_db` reads `n` as a pseudo-
location. Input n performs n + 1 nested calls (the last at depth n + 1)
and, the stack being monotonic, occupies 16(n + 1) stack cells. With
sufficient budget F_B(n) = (Σ_{i<n} db[i] mod 256, 0) for n ≤ 16 (n = 16
needs 272 cells, hence S_cells = 9 and `stack_limit ≥ 272`); for n > 16
the check at `p` faults `FAULT_UB_MEMFAULT` on the first out-of-range
byte; with small B, `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS`; with `depth_limit ≤ n` or
`stack_limit < 16(n + 1)`, `FAULT_BUDGET_DEPTH`. Hashes by §9.2: `@zero`
is a data symbol and the `zero` global's image; `@sum` is a one-member
SCC (its self-reference is written `@$0`, its `@zero` reference is
replaced by `@` + the `zero` hash, which is its only part-(6) line; its
closure set is the `zero` global's leaf and image), so its envelope is
exactly the bytes below, its `scc_hash` is their SHA-256 and its hash
is SHA-256 of the ASCII `<scc_hash hex>:0`:

```
isa=0.8
ptr_width=32
{"abi":"0.8","kind":"lproc","params":[8,8,32],"result":8,"tier":"q"}
lproc @sum (n:reg[8], acc:reg[8], base:reg[32]) (r:reg[8]) () () ()
regs { zp:reg[32], zv:reg[8], z:reg[1], one:reg[8], n2:reg[8], idx:reg[32], p:reg[32], v:reg[8], acc2:reg[8] }
^entry():
zp = lift.addr @7002ed5ea010907a0ae99065663f22fb7d18ca1d6cb171fed57e2594bd9367e6
lift.boundscheck zp 1
zv = lift.load.i8 zp
z = lift.icmp.eq n zv
qbranch z ^done ^more
^more():
one = lift.const.i8 1
n2 = lift.sub n one
idx = lift.zext.i32 n2
p = lift.add base idx
lift.boundscheck p 1
v = lift.load.i8 p
acc2 = lift.add acc v
r = lift.call @$0 (n2, acc2, base)
lift.ret r
^done():
lift.ret acc
data zero 00
layout globals.zero {"base":16,"image":"zero","size":1}
7002ed5ea010907a0ae99065663f22fb7d18ca1d6cb171fed57e2594bd9367e6
```

`@sum_db`'s envelope includes every layout leaf, the `zero` image, `@` +
the `sum` hash in place of `@sum`, and the `sum` hash as its part-(6)
line (`@db` is an interface region, not a symbol):

```
inc8 = 8ce5e64f15830d8e596ba9b4861def6565dd567b5804300f427d8b9566d5be93
zero = 7002ed5ea010907a0ae99065663f22fb7d18ca1d6cb171fed57e2594bd9367e6
sum = 74f110bbafde68a4785025e7e571ef871ddd83a09465ab9c1604f653a0cfcd92
sum_db = 68225d213c44812fe844cd295d8821127c3cf31682be4eb19303cb53f9b147f7
```

## 17. Decisions deferred to implementation, with defaults

Each item is one an implementer must decide to build; any decision is
conformant provided two implementations agree on the default below until
the item is revised. Items 1–5 are asserted non-semantic.

1. **Binary encoding.** Default: none; §16 text is the only interchange
   form.
2. **Gate-name registry.** Default: the names of §4.4 only; an unknown
   gate name is a load error.
3. **Further device models.** Default: the four of §7.3; an `effect` on
   any other device is `FAULT_EFFECT_UNMODELLED`.
4. **Mechanisation of §14.** Default: none; the reference interpreter is
   the oracle.
5. **Memory layout of the opaque C objects.** Default: opaque; only the
   listed functions touch them.
6. **Measurement-based cleanup** (§6.4): the normative fixup, its
   controlled variant and its certificate kind. Default: unitary cleanup
   (`reverse`); `capabilities.mbu` is `false`.
7. **Expansion library** (§11): the gate-level expansion below row
   level. Default: the library `ref` published by `bennett-isa-spec`
   (ripple-carry adders and comparators, linear `inrange` scans,
   one-hot address dispatch, clean scratch released in reverse order);
   a schedule that names no `expansion` binds `ref` at the ISA's own
   version.
8. **Enclosure procedure for transcendental entries** (§12.1). Default:
   Taylor series of sin and cos to the first term whose Lagrange
   remainder bound is below 2^−(`precision_bits` + 2), argument reduced
   modulo 2π with an outward-rounded enclosure of π.
9. **Default `epsilon_share`** (§8.1, §11) when a schedule assigns none.
   Default: the region's `epsilon` divided equally among its ε > 0
   operations.
10. **`any`-class resolution** (§11). Default: the first class in JCS
    order with capacity.
11. **Occupancy rate of a class absent from `rate`** (§8.2). Default: 1.
12. **Classical step timing of CC/R instructions and effects** (§8.2).
    Default: `classical_step_time` each, sequential.
13. **Suite sizes** (§15): the exhaustive widths of suite C and the
    sample counts of `sampled` claims. Default: exhaustive for ≤ 16
    interface bits; 2^16 samples above.
14. **Hardware handling of an unclean `qreg.free`** (§3.3). Default: the
    run is marked `FAILED` with a fault record `FAULT_UB_TRAP` at the
    instruction, since cleanliness of an arbitrary state is not
    testable nondestructively.

````diff
diff --git a/scripts/coverage b/scripts/coverage
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..a41ac12
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/coverage
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Summarise GCC executable-line coverage for plugin sources, without a threshold."""
+
+import argparse
+import gzip
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--build-dir", type=Path, default=ROOT / "build/coverage18")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    notes = sorted(args.build_dir.rglob("*.gcno"))
+    if not notes:
+        raise SystemExit(f"no instrumented objects under {args.build_dir}")
+    destination = ROOT / ".tmp/coverage-report"
+    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    files = {}
+    for note in notes:
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            ["gcov", "--json-format", str(note.resolve())],
+            cwd=destination,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=30,
+        )
+        if result.returncode:
+            raise SystemExit(result.stderr)
+        report = destination / (note.stem + ".gcov.json.gz")
+        with gzip.open(report, "rt") as stream:
+            data = json.load(stream)
+        for source in data["files"]:
+            path = Path(source["file"]).resolve()
+            if not path.is_relative_to(ROOT / "src"):
+                continue
+            name = str(path.relative_to(ROOT))
+            lines = files.setdefault(name, {})
+            for line in source["lines"]:
+                number = line["line_number"]
+                lines[number] = lines.get(number, 0) + line["count"]
+    rows = {
+        name: {
+            "covered": sum(count > 0 for count in lines.values()),
+            "lines": len(lines),
+        }
+        for name, lines in sorted(files.items())
+    }
+    covered = sum(row["covered"] for row in rows.values())
+    total = sum(row["lines"] for row in rows.values())
+    if not total:
+        raise SystemExit("gcov reports contain no executable plugin source lines")
+    result = {
+        "covered": covered,
+        "lines": total,
+        "percent": round(100 * covered / total, 2),
+        "files": rows,
+    }
+    (destination / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

diff --git a/scripts/quality.py b/scripts/quality.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..37f69f7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/quality.py
@@ -0,0 +1,210 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Repository-local quality proxies and a ratchet against docs/quality.md."""
+
+import argparse
+import ast
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+BASELINE = re.compile(r"<!-- quality-baseline -->\s*```json\n(.*?)\n```", re.S)
+IDENTIFIER = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:bp|bd|b-dialect-spec)-[a-z0-9]+\b|\b(?:sol|quality)-plugin\b"
+)
+LITTER = re.compile(
+    r"(^|/)(__pycache__|PROGRESS[^/]*|LAST-RUN[^/]*)(/|$)|\.(pyc|log|lock|darc)$|(^|/)LOCK$"
+)
+CONTROL = {"if", "for", "while", "switch", "catch", "sizeof", "alignas"}
+TOKENS = re.compile(
+    r'//[^\n]*|/\*.*?\*/|R"([^ ()\\\t\r\n]*)\(.*?\)\1"|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|\x27(?:\\.|[^\x27\\])*\x27',
+    re.S,
+)
+
+
+def cpp_functions(source):
+    masked = TOKENS.sub(lambda match: re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", match.group()), source)
+    stack, functions = [], []
+    for match in re.finditer(r"[{}]", masked):
+        position = match.start()
+        if match.group() == "{":
+            boundary = max(masked.rfind(char, 0, position) for char in ";{}") + 1
+            header = masked[boundary:position]
+            signature = re.search(
+                r"([A-Za-z_~]\w*)\s*\([^{};]*\)\s*(?:const|override|noexcept)?\s*$",
+                header,
+            )
+            name = signature.group(1) if signature else None
+            stack.append((position, name if name not in CONTROL else None, boundary))
+        else:
+            if not stack:
+                raise ValueError("unbalanced closing brace in C++ source")
+            start, name, boundary = stack.pop()
+            if name:
+                first = (
+                    boundary
+                    + len(masked[boundary:start])
+                    - len(masked[boundary:start].lstrip())
+                )
+                line = masked.count("\n", 0, first) + 1
+                length = masked.count("\n", first, position) + 1
+                body = masked[start + 1 : position].strip()
+                trivial = bool(re.fullmatch(r"(?:return\s+)?[\w:.]+\([^;{}]*\);", body))
+                functions.append(
+                    {"name": name, "line": line, "length": length, "trivial": trivial}
+                )
+    if stack:
+        raise ValueError("unbalanced opening brace in C++ source")
+    depth, complexity = 0, 0
+    for match in re.finditer(
+        r"\b(?:if|for|while|switch|catch|else)\b|&&|\|\||\?|[{}]", masked
+    ):
+        token = match.group()
+        if token == "{":
+            depth += 1
+        elif token == "}":
+            depth -= 1
+        else:
+            complexity += 1 + depth
+    return functions, complexity
+
+
+def python_functions(source):
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    functions = []
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
+            body = node.body
+            if (
+                body
+                and isinstance(body[0], ast.Expr)
+                and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Constant)
+                and isinstance(body[0].value.value, str)
+            ):
+                body = body[1:]
+            trivial = (
+                len(body) == 1
+                and isinstance(body[0], (ast.Return, ast.Expr))
+                and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Call)
+            )
+            functions.append(
+                {
+                    "name": node.name,
+                    "line": node.lineno,
+                    "length": node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1,
+                    "trivial": trivial,
+                }
+            )
+    branches = (
+        ast.If,
+        ast.For,
+        ast.AsyncFor,
+        ast.While,
+        ast.ExceptHandler,
+        ast.IfExp,
+        ast.Match,
+    )
+
+    def mass(node, depth=0):
+        branch = isinstance(node, branches)
+        own = 1 + depth if branch else 0
+        if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
+            own += len(node.values) - 1
+        return own + sum(
+            mass(child, depth + branch) for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node)
+        )
+
+    return functions, mass(tree)
+
+
+def measure(root, paths):
+    files, long_functions = {}, []
+    process_identifiers = 0
+    for name in sorted(paths):
+        path = root / name
+        if not path.is_file():
+            continue
+        is_python = path.suffix == ".py" or (
+            name.startswith("scripts/")
+            and not path.suffix
+            and "python" in path.read_text().partition("\n")[0]
+        )
+        if not is_python and path.suffix not in (".cpp", ".c", ".h", ".inc"):
+            continue
+        source = path.read_text()
+        if name.startswith(("src/", "include/")):
+            process_identifiers += len(IDENTIFIER.findall(source))
+        if is_python:
+            functions, complexity = python_functions(source)
+        else:
+            functions, complexity = cpp_functions(source)
+        lengths = sorted(function["length"] for function in functions)
+        percentile = lambda fraction: (
+            lengths[math.ceil(fraction * len(lengths)) - 1] if lengths else 0
+        )
+        files[name] = {
+            "functions": len(lengths),
+            "length_p50": percentile(0.5),
+            "length_p90": percentile(0.9),
+            "length_max": max(lengths, default=0),
+            "over_300": sum(length > 300 for length in lengths),
+            "complexity": complexity,
+            "trivial_wrappers": sum(function["trivial"] for function in functions),
+        }
+        long_functions.extend(
+            {"file": name, **function}
+            for function in functions
+            if function["length"] > 300
+        )
+    return {
+        "files": files,
+        "process_identifiers": process_identifiers,
+        "litter": sorted(name for name in paths if LITTER.search(name)),
+        "long_functions": long_functions,
+    }
+
+
+def regressions(current, baseline):
+    failures = []
+    for key in ("process_identifiers", "litter"):
+        count = lambda value: len(value) if isinstance(value, list) else value
+        if count(current[key]) > count(baseline[key]):
+            failures.append(f"{key}: {count(baseline[key])} -> {count(current[key])}")
+    for name, values in current["files"].items():
+        previous = baseline["files"].get(name, {})
+        for key, value in values.items():
+            if key != "functions" and value > previous.get(key, 0):
+                failures.append(f"{name} {key}: {previous.get(key, 0)} -> {value}")
+    return failures
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "ls-files", "-z"],
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        timeout=10,
+        check=True,
+    )
+    paths = result.stdout.rstrip("\0").split("\0")
+    current = measure(ROOT, paths)
+    if args.check:
+        match = BASELINE.search((ROOT / "docs/quality.md").read_text())
+        if not match:
+            raise SystemExit("docs/quality.md has no quality-baseline JSON block")
+        failures = regressions(current, json.loads(match.group(1)))
+        if failures:
+            raise SystemExit("quality baseline worsened:\n" + "\n".join(failures))
+        print("quality baseline: no regressions")
+    else:
+        print(json.dumps(current, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

diff --git a/scripts/test b/scripts/test
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..f56cf88
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/test
@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Default, bounded checks; scripts/gate also runs the slow integration drivers."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+POLICIES = ("smoke", "gate_policy", "contract_policy", "pin_policy", "quality_ratchet")
+DRIVERS = (
+    "recognition",
+    "analysis_edges",
+    "validation",
+    "scalars",
+    "address_spaces",
+    "register_classes",
+    "entry_runtime",
+    "normalisation_scope",
+)
+REGRESSIONS = (
+    "shuffle",
+    "byval",
+    "global-diagnostic",
+    "byte-order",
+    "native-abi",
+    "block-order",
+    "control",
+    "dynamic-gate",
+    "unresolved-call",
+)
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--major", action="append", type=int, choices=(18, 23))
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    environment = dict(os.environ)
+    for key in ("DISPLAY", "WAYLAND_DISPLAY", "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS", "BROWSER"):
+        environment.pop(key, None)
+    temporary = ROOT / ".tmp/tests"
+    temporary.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    environment.setdefault("TMPDIR", str(temporary))
+    environment["PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE"] = "1"
+    commands = [[sys.executable, "-B", f"tests/{name}.py"] for name in POLICIES]
+    for major in args.major or (18, 23):
+        commands.extend(
+            [sys.executable, "-B", f"tests/{name}.py", "--major", str(major)]
+            for name in DRIVERS
+        )
+        commands.append(
+            [
+                sys.executable,
+                "-B",
+                "tests/review_regressions.py",
+                "--major",
+                str(major),
+                *(argument for name in REGRESSIONS for argument in ("--case", name)),
+            ]
+        )
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    for command in commands:
+        remaining = 180 - (time.monotonic() - started)
+        if remaining <= 0:
+            raise SystemExit("default tests exceeded the 180-second allowance")
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            command,
+            cwd=ROOT,
+            env=environment,
+            text=True,
+            capture_output=True,
+            timeout=min(120, remaining),
+        )
+        label = " ".join(command[2:])
+        print(f"{label}: exit {result.returncode}", flush=True)
+        if result.returncode:
+            print(result.stdout)
+            print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
+            return result.returncode
+    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
+    receipt = {"commands": len(commands), "elapsed_s": round(elapsed, 3)}
+    (temporary / "default.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps(receipt))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+// Discover source state while every reachable entry still has its original body.
+bool sharesGlobalState(Function &f) {
+  std::set<const Value *> visited;
+  bool sharedState = false;
+  std::function<void(const Value *)> findState = [&](const Value *value) {
+    if (!visited.insert(value).second) return;
+    if (auto *function = dyn_cast<Function>(value)) {
+      if (!function->isDeclaration())
+        for (const auto &instruction : instructions(function)) findState(&instruction);
+      return;
+    }
+    if (auto *global = dyn_cast<GlobalVariable>(value)) {
+      sharedState |= !global->isConstant();
+      if (global->hasInitializer()) findState(global->getInitializer());
+      return;
+    }
+    if (auto *user = dyn_cast<User>(value))
+      for (const auto &operand : user->operands()) findState(operand);
+  };
+  findState(&f);
+  return sharedState;
+}
````

## `CMakeLists.txt` (63 lines)

````
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(bennett-plugin LANGUAGES C CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
option(BENNETT_COVERAGE "Instrument a single LLVM-major GCC build with gcov" OFF)
if(BENNETT_COVERAGE AND NOT LLVM_DIR)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "Set LLVM_DIR to select one major for coverage")
endif()
if(NOT LLVM_DIR)
  include(ExternalProject)
  foreach(major 18 23)
    ExternalProject_Add(llvm${major}
      SOURCE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}"
      BINARY_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/llvm${major}"
      CMAKE_ARGS -DLLVM_DIR=/usr/lib/llvm-${major}/lib/cmake/llvm
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBENNETT_OUTPUT_DIR=${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}
      INSTALL_COMMAND "" BUILD_ALWAYS TRUE)
  endforeach()
else()
  find_package(LLVM REQUIRED CONFIG)
  if(NOT LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR MATCHES "^(18|23)$")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Tested LLVM majors are 18 and 23")
  endif()
  add_library(BennettPlugin MODULE src/BennettPlugin.cpp src/NativeComparison.cpp src/Analysis.cpp src/Scalar.cpp src/Normalise.cpp src/SoftFloat.cpp src/Wide.cpp src/Integer.cpp src/Memory.cpp src/Residual.cpp src/Production.cpp src/Snapshot.cpp)
  if(BENNETT_COVERAGE)
    if(NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL "GNU")
      message(FATAL_ERROR "BENNETT_COVERAGE requires GCC and matching gcov")
    endif()
    target_compile_options(BennettPlugin PRIVATE --coverage -O0 -g1)
    target_link_options(BennettPlugin PRIVATE --coverage)
  endif()
  target_include_directories(BennettPlugin SYSTEM PRIVATE ${LLVM_INCLUDE_DIRS})
  target_compile_definitions(BennettPlugin PRIVATE ${LLVM_DEFINITIONS})
  set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/SPEC_VERSIONS.toml"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/gate.toml"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/contracts.py"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/pinned_siblings.py")
  find_package(Python3 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Interpreter)
  execute_process(
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}" -c
      "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1] + '/tests'); from contracts import arith_path; print(arith_path(int(sys.argv[2])).absolute())"
      "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}" "${LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR}"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}"
    RESULT_VARIABLE arith_status OUTPUT_VARIABLE arith_path ERROR_VARIABLE arith_error
    OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE)
  if(NOT arith_status STREQUAL "0")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Pinned arithmetic LLVM ${LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR} unavailable:\n${arith_error}")
  endif()
  file(READ "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/SPEC_VERSIONS.toml" spec_pins)
  string(REGEX MATCH "llvm${LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR}_sha256 = \"([^\"]+)\"" arith_pin "${spec_pins}")
  if(NOT arith_pin)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Missing arith LLVM ${LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR} sha256 pin")
  endif()
  set(arith_sha256 "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
  target_compile_definitions(BennettPlugin PRIVATE
    BENNETT_ARITH_DEFAULT_PATH="${arith_path}"
    BENNETT_ARITH_DEFAULT_SHA256="${arith_sha256}")
  set_target_properties(BennettPlugin PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME bennett-plugin-${LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR})
  if(BENNETT_OUTPUT_DIR)
    set_target_properties(BennettPlugin PROPERTIES LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${BENNETT_OUTPUT_DIR}")
  endif()
endif()
````

````
from pathlib import Path
R=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
for key in ['DISPLAY','WAYLAND_DISPLAY','DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS','BROWSER']: os.environ.pop(key,None)
(R/'.tmp').mkdir(exist_ok=True);os.environ.setdefault('TMPDIR',str(R/'.tmp'))
sys.path.insert(0, str(R/'tests'))
from contracts import arith_path
arith_paths={major:arith_path(major) for major in (18,23)}
if shutil.which('cmake'):
 subprocess.run(['cmake','-S',str(R),'-B',str(R/'build')],check=True)
 subprocess.run(['cmake','--build',str(R/'build'),'-j','3'],check=True)
else:
 print('cmake unavailable: offline llvm-config build (CMake configuration unverified)',flush=True)
 pins=tomllib.loads((R/'SPEC_VERSIONS.toml').read_text())['arith']
 def build(major):
  tool=Path(f'/usr/lib/llvm-{major}/bin')
  flags=subprocess.check_output([str(tool/'llvm-config'),'--cxxflags'],text=True).split()
  definitions=[f'-DBENNETT_ARITH_DEFAULT_PATH="{arith_paths[major]}"',
               f'-DBENNETT_ARITH_DEFAULT_SHA256="{pins[f"llvm{major}_sha256"]}"']
  compile_flags=[*flags,'-std=c++17','-fPIC','-g','-O2',*definitions]
  dest=R/f'build/llvm{major}';dest.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
  objs=[]
  for src in sorted((R/'src').glob('*.cpp')):
   obj=dest/(src.stem+'.o');objs.append(str(obj))
   digest=hashlib.sha256(src.read_bytes()+(R/'src/Bennett.h').read_bytes()+'\0'.join(compile_flags).encode()).hexdigest()
   stamp=obj.with_suffix('.sha256')
   if not obj.exists() or not stamp.exists() or stamp.read_text()!=digest:
    subprocess.run(['g++',*compile_flags,'-c',str(src),'-o',str(obj)],check=True)
    stamp.write_text(digest)
  output=R/f'build/libbennett-plugin-{major}.so'
  temporary=output.with_suffix('.so.new')
  subprocess.run(['g++','-shared',*objs,'-o',str(temporary)],check=True)
  temporary.replace(output)
 with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:list(pool.map(build,[18,23]))
````

````
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarise GCC executable-line coverage for plugin sources, without a threshold."""

import argparse
import gzip
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--build-dir", type=Path, default=ROOT / "build/coverage18")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    notes = sorted(args.build_dir.rglob("*.gcno"))
    if not notes:
        raise SystemExit(f"no instrumented objects under {args.build_dir}")
    destination = ROOT / ".tmp/coverage-report"
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = {}
    for note in notes:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["gcov", "--json-format", str(note.resolve())],
            cwd=destination,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
        )
        if result.returncode:
            raise SystemExit(result.stderr)
        report = destination / (note.stem + ".gcov.json.gz")
        with gzip.open(report, "rt") as stream:
            data = json.load(stream)
        for source in data["files"]:
            path = Path(source["file"]).resolve()
            if not path.is_relative_to(ROOT / "src"):
                continue
            name = str(path.relative_to(ROOT))
            lines = files.setdefault(name, {})
            for line in source["lines"]:
                number = line["line_number"]
                lines[number] = lines.get(number, 0) + line["count"]
    rows = {
        name: {
            "covered": sum(count > 0 for count in lines.values()),
            "lines": len(lines),
        }
        for name, lines in sorted(files.items())
    }
    covered = sum(row["covered"] for row in rows.values())
    total = sum(row["lines"] for row in rows.values())
    if not total:
        raise SystemExit("gcov reports contain no executable plugin source lines")
    result = {
        "covered": covered,
        "lines": total,
        "percent": round(100 * covered / total, 2),
        "files": rows,
    }
    (destination / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Repository-local quality proxies and a ratchet against docs/quality.md."""

import argparse
import ast
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BASELINE = re.compile(r"<!-- quality-baseline -->\s*```json\n(.*?)\n```", re.S)
IDENTIFIER = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:bp|bd|b-dialect-spec)-[a-z0-9]+\b|\b(?:sol|quality)-plugin\b"
)
LITTER = re.compile(
    r"(^|/)(__pycache__|PROGRESS[^/]*|LAST-RUN[^/]*)(/|$)|\.(pyc|log|lock|darc)$|(^|/)LOCK$"
)
CONTROL = {"if", "for", "while", "switch", "catch", "sizeof", "alignas"}
TOKENS = re.compile(
    r'//[^\n]*|/\*.*?\*/|R"([^ ()\\\t\r\n]*)\(.*?\)\1"|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|\x27(?:\\.|[^\x27\\])*\x27',
    re.S,
)


def cpp_functions(source):
    masked = TOKENS.sub(lambda match: re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", match.group()), source)
    stack, functions = [], []
    for match in re.finditer(r"[{}]", masked):
        position = match.start()
        if match.group() == "{":
            boundary = max(masked.rfind(char, 0, position) for char in ";{}") + 1
            header = masked[boundary:position]
            signature = re.search(
                r"([A-Za-z_~]\w*)\s*\([^{};]*\)\s*(?:const|override|noexcept)?\s*$",
                header,
            )
            name = signature.group(1) if signature else None
            stack.append((position, name if name not in CONTROL else None, boundary))
        else:
            if not stack:
                raise ValueError("unbalanced closing brace in C++ source")
            start, name, boundary = stack.pop()
            if name:
                first = (
                    boundary
                    + len(masked[boundary:start])
                    - len(masked[boundary:start].lstrip())
                )
                line = masked.count("\n", 0, first) + 1
                length = masked.count("\n", first, position) + 1
                body = masked[start + 1 : position].strip()
                trivial = bool(re.fullmatch(r"(?:return\s+)?[\w:.]+\([^;{}]*\);", body))
                functions.append(
                    {"name": name, "line": line, "length": length, "trivial": trivial}
                )
    if stack:
        raise ValueError("unbalanced opening brace in C++ source")
    depth, complexity = 0, 0
    for match in re.finditer(
        r"\b(?:if|for|while|switch|catch|else)\b|&&|\|\||\?|[{}]", masked
    ):
        token = match.group()
        if token == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif token == "}":
            depth -= 1
        else:
            complexity += 1 + depth
    return functions, complexity


def python_functions(source):
    tree = ast.parse(source)
    functions = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            body = node.body
            if (
                body
                and isinstance(body[0], ast.Expr)
                and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Constant)
                and isinstance(body[0].value.value, str)
            ):
                body = body[1:]
            trivial = (
                len(body) == 1
                and isinstance(body[0], (ast.Return, ast.Expr))
                and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Call)
            )
            functions.append(
                {
                    "name": node.name,
                    "line": node.lineno,
                    "length": node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1,
                    "trivial": trivial,
                }
            )
    branches = (
        ast.If,
        ast.For,
        ast.AsyncFor,
        ast.While,
        ast.ExceptHandler,
        ast.IfExp,
        ast.Match,
    )

    def mass(node, depth=0):
        branch = isinstance(node, branches)
        own = 1 + depth if branch else 0
        if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
            own += len(node.values) - 1
        return own + sum(
            mass(child, depth + branch) for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node)
        )

    return functions, mass(tree)


def measure(root, paths):
    files, long_functions = {}, []
    process_identifiers = 0
    for name in sorted(paths):
        path = root / name
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        is_python = path.suffix == ".py" or (
            name.startswith("scripts/")
            and not path.suffix
            and "python" in path.read_text().partition("\n")[0]
        )
        if not is_python and path.suffix not in (".cpp", ".c", ".h", ".inc"):
            continue
        source = path.read_text()
        if name.startswith(("src/", "include/")):
            process_identifiers += len(IDENTIFIER.findall(source))
        if is_python:
            functions, complexity = python_functions(source)
        else:
            functions, complexity = cpp_functions(source)
        lengths = sorted(function["length"] for function in functions)
        percentile = lambda fraction: (
            lengths[math.ceil(fraction * len(lengths)) - 1] if lengths else 0
        )
        files[name] = {
            "functions": len(lengths),
            "length_p50": percentile(0.5),
            "length_p90": percentile(0.9),
            "length_max": max(lengths, default=0),
            "over_300": sum(length > 300 for length in lengths),
            "complexity": complexity,
            "trivial_wrappers": sum(function["trivial"] for function in functions),
        }
        long_functions.extend(
            {"file": name, **function}
            for function in functions
            if function["length"] > 300
        )
    return {
        "files": files,
        "process_identifiers": process_identifiers,
        "litter": sorted(name for name in paths if LITTER.search(name)),
        "long_functions": long_functions,
    }


def regressions(current, baseline):
    failures = []
    for key in ("process_identifiers", "litter"):
        count = lambda value: len(value) if isinstance(value, list) else value
        if count(current[key]) > count(baseline[key]):
            failures.append(f"{key}: {count(baseline[key])} -> {count(current[key])}")
    for name, values in current["files"].items():
        previous = baseline["files"].get(name, {})
        for key, value in values.items():
            if key != "functions" and value > previous.get(key, 0):
                failures.append(f"{name} {key}: {previous.get(key, 0)} -> {value}")
    return failures


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files", "-z"],
        cwd=ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=10,
        check=True,
    )
    paths = result.stdout.rstrip("\0").split("\0")
    current = measure(ROOT, paths)
    if args.check:
        match = BASELINE.search((ROOT / "docs/quality.md").read_text())
        if not match:
            raise SystemExit("docs/quality.md has no quality-baseline JSON block")
        failures = regressions(current, json.loads(match.group(1)))
        if failures:
            raise SystemExit("quality baseline worsened:\n" + "\n".join(failures))
        print("quality baseline: no regressions")
    else:
        print(json.dumps(current, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Record the latest gate pass into docs/verification.json.

The file keeps only the latest pass.
Full history: `git log -p docs/verification.json`.

Evidence comes from a completed gate run: <root>/.tmp/*.json written by tests/*.py and
<root>/build/*.so. Run the gate first (scripts/gate in the tree), then for example:

  scripts/record-verification.py --pass ninth --date 2026-11-01 --commits abc1234,def5678 --gate-exit 0
"""
import argparse, datetime, hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
R = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(R / 'tests'))
from contracts import PIN, sibling, dialect_text, drift

MAJORS = (18, 23)
ISA_REF = sibling('bennett-isa-spec') / 'reference-interpreter/target/debug/bennett-isa-ref'
SUMMARY_KEYS = ('cases_run', 'cases_agree', 'cases_deferred', 'cases_blocked', 'cases_diverge')


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def gate_counts(summary):
    """run/agree/deferred/blocked/diverge plus cells, per major."""
    return {str(m): '/'.join(str(summary[str(m)][k]) for k in SUMMARY_KEYS) +
            f" cells {summary[str(m)]['cells_agree']}/{summary[str(m)]['cells_run']}" for m in MAJORS}


def check_rows(rows):
    """Count rows whose own recorded verdicts all hold (checks, runs, rejections)."""
    ok = 0
    for r in rows:
        good = r.get('ok', True) and r.get('check', True) and r.get('run', True)
        good = good and all(x.get('ok', True) for x in r.get('runs', []))
        good = good and r.get('common_failure', True)
        ok += bool(good)
    return {'cases': len(rows), 'ok': ok, 'expected_rejections': sum(bool(r.get('expected_rejection')) for r in rows)}


def object_paths(tmp, major, scalars):
    """(name, path) of every emitted object whose cross-major equality is recorded."""
    out = []
    for o in scalars['objects']:
        if o.get('lowered'):
            out.append((f"scalar/{o['name']}", tmp / f"scalars/{major}/{o['name']}/ref.bennett"))
    out.append(('scalar/c-O3-inc8', tmp / f'scalars/{major}/c-inc8/ref.bennett'))
    out.append(('descriptor-reference/inc8', tmp / f'descriptors/{major}/oracle-0/ref.bennett'))
    for rel in ('top/launch.bennett', 'top/oracle-0/ref.bennett'):
        out.append((f'descriptor-production/{rel}', tmp / f'descriptors/{major}/production/{rel}'))
    for case in ('0', '7', '255', 'published'):
        for rel in ('launch.bennett', 'oracle-0/ref.bennett'):
            out.append((f'production/{case}/{rel}', tmp / f'production/{major}/{case}/out/top/{rel}'))
    out.append(('production/abi/launch.bennett', tmp / f'production/{major}/abi/out/abi/launch.bennett'))
    for family in ('production-shapes', 'production-budgets', 'production-dispatch', 'production-environments', 'production-lifts', 'shadow-stack', 'budget-stage', 'entry-snapshot', 'softfloat', 'wide', 'integer-intrinsics', 'memory-runtime', 'aggregate-rows', 'cc-calls', 'cc-switch', 'reversible'):
        base = tmp / f'{family}/{major}'
        for p in sorted(base.rglob('*.bennett')):
            if family=='reversible' and 'r-hello' in p.relative_to(base).parts: continue
            out.append((f'{family}/{p.relative_to(base)}', p))
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--pass', dest='name', required=True, help='pass name, e.g. ninth')
    ap.add_argument('--date', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--commits', required=True, help='comma-separated landed commits')
    ap.add_argument('--gate-exit', type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--root', type=Path, default=R, help='tree whose .tmp/ and build/ the gate used')
    ap.add_argument('--rung3-report', type=Path, help='consumer report, including failed prerequisite rows')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    assert a.gate_exit == 0, 'refusing to record a failed gate'
    tmp, build = a.root / '.tmp', a.root / 'build'
    read = lambda name: json.loads((tmp / name).read_text())
    assert not drift(), 'accepted contract drift'
    gate = read('corpus-gate.json')
    assert gate['dialect_commit'] == PIN and not gate['accepted_contract_drift']
    for major, h in gate['plugin_sha256'].items():
        assert digest(build / f'libbennett-plugin-{major}.so') == h, f'plugin {major} changed after the gate'
    for m in MAJORS:
        s = gate['summary'][str(m)]
        assert [s[k] for k in SUMMARY_KEYS]==[66,66,0,0,0], (m,s)

    checks, scalars = {}, {}
    for m in MAJORS:
        c = {}
        for name in ('recognition', 'analysis-edges', 'analysis-performance', 'reference-images', 'materialisation', 'aggregate-rows', 'allocator-closure', 'cc-calls', 'cc-switch', 'reversible', 'softfloat', 'wide', 'integer-intrinsics', 'memory-runtime', 'region-keys', 'validation'):
            j = read(f'{name}-{m}.json')
            assert j['passed'] == j['cases'], (name, m)
            c[name] = {'cases': j['cases'], 'passed': j['passed']}
            if name in ('aggregate-rows','allocator-closure','cc-calls', 'cc-switch', 'reversible'):c[name]['evidence']=j['results']
            if name=='analysis-performance':
                c[name].update(seconds=j['seconds'],rounds=j['rounds'],budget_diagnostic=j['budget_diagnostic'])
            if name=='softfloat':
                c[name]['known_remainders']=[r for r in j['results'] if r.get('expected_unimplemented')]
                c[name]['native_wide']=[r for r in j['results'] if r['name'].startswith('published-native-wide-')]
                c[name]['recursive_closure']=[r for r in j['results'] if r['name'].startswith('CC-recursive-')]
                c[name]['closure_contract'] = {
                    'rewrite': '§13.1: The entry points are defined by bennett-arith and are part of its bitcode the driver links.',
                    'recursion': '§14.1: Direct calls lower to CC/R call; Recursion is unrestricted.',
                    'transport': '§17.4: LLVM integer and memory instructions map to ISA instructions; phis to block parameters; multi-result calls carry aggregates.',
                    'original_stop': '§13.1 recursive CC soft-float closure: active-set inlining guard at bennett_sf_eval',
                    'llvm23_recursive_instruction': 'call void @bennett_sf_eval(ptr %19, i32 %1, i32 3, ptr %18, i32 0, i32 %5)',
                    'cc_steps_note': 'run-program reports CC steps separately from the nested oracle; successful unchanged 64-wire launch uses two 1000000-step oracle tokens. L numerical rows record nested materialised steps.'}

                c[name]['published_production']=[r for r in j['results'] if r['name'].startswith('published-production')]
        audit = read(f'key-audit-{m}.json')
        assert not audit['unaccounted'] and audit['accounted'] == audit['unmatched']
        c['full-key-audit'] = {k: audit[k] for k in ('cases', 'matched', 'unmatched', 'accounted', 'unaccounted')}
        d = read(f'descriptors-{m}.json')
        assert d['descriptor_inc8_equal'] and d['production_complete'] and d['production_exit'] == 0
        c['descriptors'] = {'descriptor_inc8_equal': True, 'production_complete': True}
        p = read(f'production-{m}.json')
        assert p['passed'] == 3 and p['published_oracle_inc8']['ok'] and p['native_abi']['ok']
        c['production'] = check_rows(p['cases'])
        for fam in ('dispatch', 'environments', 'shapes', 'budgets', 'records', 'lifts'):
            c[f'production-{fam}'] = check_rows(read(f'production-{fam}-{m}.json')['cases'])
            assert c[f'production-{fam}']['cases'] == c[f'production-{fam}']['ok'], (fam, m)
        snapshot = read(f'entry-snapshot-{m}.json')
        assert snapshot['cases'] and all(r.get('ok') and r.get('check') for r in snapshot['cases'])
        c['entry-snapshot'] = check_rows(snapshot['cases'])
        c['entry-snapshot']['isa_ref'] = snapshot['isa_ref']
        c['entry-snapshot']['isa_ref_sha256'] = snapshot['isa_ref_sha256']
        ss = read(f'shadow-stack-{m}.json')
        assert all(r.get('check') and r.get('ok') for r in ss['cases'])
        c['shadow-stack'] = check_rows(ss['cases'])
        stage = read(f'budget-stage-{m}.json')
        assert all(r.get('ok') and r.get('check') for r in stage['cases'])
        assert all(r['ok'] for r in stage['proof_cases'])
        final = next(r for r in stage['cases'] if r['name'] == 'identity-once')
        assert final['reference_exact'] and final['prefix_vectors'] == 316 and final['prefixes_ok'] and final['tokens_final']
        shape = final['build']['budget_table']['shapes'][0]
        c['budget-stage'] = dict(check_rows(stage['cases']), proof_cases=len(stage['proof_cases']),
                                prefix_vectors=316, reference_exact=True, tokens_final=True,
                                selection_identity=shape['selection_identity'], identity=shape['identity'])
        checks[str(m)] = c
        sc = read(f'scalars-{m}.json')
        assert sc['c_inc8_equal'] and sc['passed'] == 21
        lowered = [o for o in sc['objects'] if o.get('lowered')]
        assert all(o['check'] and o['fixture_equal'] and o['hash_fixture_equal'] and all(r['ok'] for r in o['runs']) for o in lowered)
        scalars[str(m)] = {'objects_byte_exact': len(lowered), 'run_vectors': sum(len(o['runs']) for o in lowered),
                           'deferred': sc['deferred'], 'c_inc8_equal': True}
    assert scalars['18'] == scalars['23']

    fixtures = {n: b.encode() for n, b in re.findall(r'```isa object=([^\n ]+)\n(.*?)```', dialect_text(), re.S)}
    for size in (16, 32):
        fixtures[f'budget-stage-{size}'] = (R / f'tests/fixtures/budget-stage-{size}.bennett').read_bytes()
    sc18 = read('scalars-18.json')
    by_major = {m: dict(object_paths(tmp, m, sc18)) for m in MAJORS}
    assert by_major[18].keys() == by_major[23].keys()
    rows = []
    for name, p18 in by_major[18].items():
        data = p18.read_bytes()
        assert data == by_major[23][name].read_bytes(), f'{name}: LLVM 18/23 bytes differ'
        golden = next((g for g, b in fixtures.items() if b == data), None)
        rows.append({'object': name, 'bytes': len(data), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), 'published_golden': golden})
    cross = read('production-cross-major.json')
    assert cross['byte_identical']
    # Independent check of every launch object (CC lowering is plugin-defined, 17.4: no published golden).
    for name, p18 in by_major[18].items():
        if name.endswith('launch.bennett'):
            r = subprocess.run([str(ISA_REF), 'check', str(p18)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
            assert r.returncode == 0, (name, r.stderr)

    path = R / 'docs/verification.json'
    baseline = json.loads(path.read_text()).get('latest_pass', {}).get('object_pairs', {}).get('rows', []) if path.exists() else []
    current = {r['object']: r for r in rows}
    for old in baseline:
        assert old['object'] in current and old['sha256'] == current[old['object']]['sha256'], f"previously recorded object changed: {old['object']}"
    head = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(a.root), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip()
    latest = {
        'name': a.name, 'date': a.date, 'commits': a.commits.split(','), 'code_head': head,
        'recorded_at': datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec='seconds'),
        'dialect': '0.2.13', 'dialect_commit': PIN, 'isa': '0.8',
        'arith': __import__('tomllib').loads((R/'SPEC_VERSIONS.toml').read_text())['arith'],
        'arith_gate_paths': {str(m):str(__import__('contracts').arith_path(m)) for m in MAJORS},
        'allocator_gate_root': str(sibling('bennett-runtimes') / 'dist'),
        'plugin_sha256': gate['plugin_sha256'],
        'gate': {'command': 'scripts/gate', 'exit': a.gate_exit, 'accepted_contract_drift': False,
                 'contract_head_drift': gate['contract_head_drift'], 'contract_worktree_drift': gate['contract_worktree_drift'],
                 'corpus': gate_counts(gate['summary']),
                 'non_agreeing': [{k: r[k] for k in ('case', 'major', 'pipeline', 'classification')}
                                  for r in gate['cells'] if r['classification'] != 'agree']},
        'checks': checks, 'scalars': scalars,
        'rung2_analysis': json.loads((R/'docs/rung2-analysis.json').read_text()),
        'object_pairs': {'count': len(rows), 'byte_identical': True,
                         'published_matches': sum(bool(r['published_golden']) for r in rows),
                         'production_cross_major_pairs': cross['pairs'], 'preserved_previous_objects': len(baseline), 'rows': rows},
    }
    if a.rung3_report:
        report = json.loads(a.rung3_report.read_text())
        latest['rung3'] = {'source_report': str(a.rung3_report.resolve()),
                          'source_report_sha256': digest(a.rung3_report),
                          'exit': int(any(row['status'] != 'PASS' for stages in report['stages'].values() for row in stages.values())),
                          'report': report}
    if a.name == 'bp-ivy' and (tmp/'r-hello23-execution.json').is_file():
        obj = tmp/'reversible/23/r-hello/out/main/launch.bennett'
        checked = read('r-hello23-check.log')
        assert checked['object_hash'] == digest(obj), 'exploratory object changed after execution'
        latest['whole_program_r_exploratory'] = {
            'major': 23, 'classification': 'measured failure, not corpus agreement',
            'object_sha256': digest(obj), 'admission': checked['status'],
            'command': ['bennett-isa-spec/reference-interpreter/target/release/bennett-isa-ref',
                        'run-program', str(obj), 'main', '--budget', '10000000,1048576,65536,256',
                        '--replies', str(tmp/'reversible/23/r-console/argv.json')],
            'result': read('r-hello23-execution.json'),
            'execution_log_sha256': digest(tmp/'r-hello23-execution.json')}
    failed_logs = sorted(tmp.glob('bp-ivy-gate-*-red.log'))
    latest['prior_failed_attempts'] = [{'log': str(p.relative_to(a.root)), 'sha256': digest(p)} for p in failed_logs]
    path.write_text(json.dumps({'schema': 2, 'latest_pass': latest}, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(f"recorded pass {a.name}: {len(rows)} object pairs, {latest['object_pairs']['published_matches']} published matches, "
          "latest pass only")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
````

````
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Default, bounded checks; scripts/gate also runs the slow integration drivers."""

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
POLICIES = ("smoke", "gate_policy", "contract_policy", "pin_policy", "quality_ratchet")
DRIVERS = (
    "recognition",
    "analysis_edges",
    "validation",
    "scalars",
    "address_spaces",
    "register_classes",
    "entry_runtime",
    "normalisation_scope",
)
REGRESSIONS = (
    "shuffle",
    "byval",
    "global-diagnostic",
    "byte-order",
    "native-abi",
    "block-order",
    "control",
    "dynamic-gate",
    "unresolved-call",
)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--major", action="append", type=int, choices=(18, 23))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    environment = dict(os.environ)
    for key in ("DISPLAY", "WAYLAND_DISPLAY", "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS", "BROWSER"):
        environment.pop(key, None)
    temporary = ROOT / ".tmp/tests"
    temporary.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    environment.setdefault("TMPDIR", str(temporary))
    environment["PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE"] = "1"
    commands = [[sys.executable, "-B", f"tests/{name}.py"] for name in POLICIES]
    for major in args.major or (18, 23):
        commands.extend(
            [sys.executable, "-B", f"tests/{name}.py", "--major", str(major)]
            for name in DRIVERS
        )
        commands.append(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-B",
                "tests/review_regressions.py",
                "--major",
                str(major),
                *(argument for name in REGRESSIONS for argument in ("--case", name)),
            ]
        )
    started = time.monotonic()
    for command in commands:
        remaining = 180 - (time.monotonic() - started)
        if remaining <= 0:
            raise SystemExit("default tests exceeded the 180-second allowance")
        result = subprocess.run(
            command,
            cwd=ROOT,
            env=environment,
            text=True,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=min(120, remaining),
        )
        label = " ".join(command[2:])
        print(f"{label}: exit {result.returncode}", flush=True)
        if result.returncode:
            print(result.stdout)
            print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
            return result.returncode
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
    receipt = {"commands": len(commands), "elapsed_s": round(elapsed, 3)}
    (temporary / "default.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(receipt))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
````

````
[[noreturn]] void fail(StringRef code, StringRef section, const Value *v) {
  errs() << "bennett: " << code << ": " << section;
  if (v) {
    errs() << " at ";
    v->print(errs());
  }
  errs() << "\n";
  std::exit(1);
}

const std::map<std::string, std::string> &markers() {

      {"__bennett_effect_entropy_read", "vpn"},

      {"__bennett_effect_block_write", "vnp"}};

    names["__bennett_ctrl_v"] = "vnpnn";
````
